\\n\\ud83d\\udcdd Walkthrough\\n\\n## Walkthrough\\n\\nAdds combo rarity, unlock cost, and level progression to combos; new ScriptableObjects and editor tooling for rarity data; Memory gains unlock/level persistence helpers; UI updated to render locked/special combos via a new SpecialComboCell and rarity visuals.\\n\\n## Changes\\n\\n|Cohort / File(s)|Summary|\\n|---|---|\\n|**Core Combo Definition**

content.content: {"result":"{\"documentId\": \"f_8fb667cfb8d1e8dcc7a182\", \"title\": \"Combo Fighter GDD\", \"revisionId\": \"8fb667cfb8\", \"text\": \"Overview\\n1. Game Overview\\nTitle: Combo Fighter\\nGenre: Merge puzzle auto battler\\nPlatform: (iOS / Android)\\nCore Loop Summary:\\nPlace fight-action tetris shaped pieces on a game board and watch the character fight hordes of enemies.\\n2. Core Gameplay\\nPlayer Actions:\\nDrag tetris shaped pieces onto the game board, merge pieces to upgrade them, connect the pieces to create combos to deal extra damage, fill the board with more pieces to deal more attacks and/or damage.\\nDraw additional pieces randomly to place them on the board. Optimize your spaces and combo connections.\\nGain experience by defeating monsters and merging tiles. Experience levels up the hero and the player can choose a skill upgrade.\\nWhen the game ends, the player can upgrade the hero's Max HP, HP regen rate during the game, and attack power.\\nGame Objective:\\nDefeat all the waves of monsters in each level.\\nFailure Condition:\\nThe player\\u2019s HP reaches 0 from monster attacks.\\n3. Game Flow\\nHome Screen: Start button, current level displayed, three upgrade buttons.\\nGameplay: 4 to 5 minutes per level. The game switches from preparation phase to battle phase with occasional pop up dialogue for roguelite skill upgrades.\\nResult Screen: Displays rewards earned. Gold only in MVP.\\nUpgrades: Hero\\u2019s Max HP, HP regen rate, hero\\u2019s attack power bonus\\n4. Level Design\\n35 hand crafted levels in MVP\\nMonsters will have increased HP and attack damage as level progresses.\\nLevels will have obstacles on the board to create difficulty. These obstacles can be removed with silver earned in the level. These obstacles reset each game.\\nLevels will have different starting points for first combo piece placement. Each level will also have a set of possible pieces that can be dropped and their drop rate.\\n5. Art & Visual Style\\nThe top portion of the screen is dedicated to combat visualization during battle phase, the bottom portion only displays the puzzle board.\\nDuring intermission between waves of monsters, the camera shifts down to reveal a puzzle board + three slots staging area for players to obtain new puzzle pieces, this is the preparation phase. Pressing a FIGHT button will shift the camera back up and transition into the battle phase.\\nCharacter Designs: Simple Chibi style 3D characters.\\nUI: Simple standard UI, home screen with minimal buttons.\\n6. Audio\\nMusic: None\\nSFX: Standard fighting sounds.\\n7. Monetization\\nAds: None in MVP\\n8. 1. Game Overview
Title: Combo Fighter
Genre: Merge puzzle auto battler
Platform: (iOS / Android)
Core Loop Summary:
Place fight-action tetris shaped pieces on a game board and watch the character fight hordes of enemies.
2. Core Gameplay
Player Actions:
Drag tetris shaped pieces onto the game board, merge pieces to upgrade them, connect the pieces to create combos to deal extra damage, fill the board with more pieces to deal more attacks and/or damage.
Draw additional pieces randomly to place them on the board. Optimize your spaces and combo connections.
Gain experience by defeating monsters and merging tiles. Experience levels up the hero and the player can choose a skill upgrade.
When the game ends, the player can upgrade the hero's Max HP, HP regen rate during the game, and attack power.
Game Objective:
Defeat all the waves of monsters in each level.
Failure Condition:
The player’s HP reaches 0 from monster attacks.
3. Game Flow
Home Screen: Start button, current level displayed, three upgrade buttons.
Gameplay: 4 to 5 minutes per level. The game switches from preparation phase to battle phase with occasional pop up dialogue for roguelite skill upgrades.
Result Screen: Displays rewards earned. Gold only in MVP.
Upgrades: Hero’s Max HP, HP regen rate, hero’s attack power bonus
4. Level Design
35 hand crafted levels in MVP
Monsters will have increased HP and attack damage as level progresses.
Levels will have obstacles on the board to create difficulty. These obstacles can be removed with silver earned in the level. These obstacles reset each game.
Levels will have different starting points for first combo piece placement. Each level will also have a set of possible pieces that can be dropped and their drop rate.
5. Art & Visual Style
The top portion of the screen is dedicated to combat visualization during battle phase, the bottom portion only displays the puzzle board.
During intermission between waves of monsters, the camera shifts down to reveal a puzzle board + three slots staging area for players to obtain new puzzle pieces, this is the preparation phase. Pressing a FIGHT button will shift the camera back up and transition into the battle phase.
Character Designs: Simple Chibi style 3D characters.
UI: Simple standard UI, home screen with minimal buttons.
6. Audio
Music: None
SFX: Standard fighting sounds.
7. Monetization
Ads: None in MVP
8. Ugly Game Mockups
Home Screen with 3 upgrade choices, start button, coin balance and settings button
Gameplay
Game Starts, 3 pieces randomly selected for players to choose from.
Players drag pieces onto the board, the character starts doing loop animation of the attacks on the board.
The values showing total punch, kick and special attack power changes real time based on pieces on the board
The dmg/s calculation also updates real time as pieces are being placed
The Info button will bring up a pop up of available moves (see below)
Pressing refresh will consume gold if available, and refreshes the 3 cards.
Holding a tile under the finger will change the refresh button to SELL. If a player moves pieces over the sell button, the piece will be sold.
Coin balance and health is displayed near the top
After pressing the fight button, the camera shifts upward to increase the size of the fight scene and the battle starts. This phase requires no input action from the players
Info Pop Up
Simple End Game Screen
DOCUMENT DOES NOT END HERE! MAKE SURE TO CLICK ON THE OTHER TABS (“Detailed Mechanics”) IN THIS DOCUMENT ON THE LEFT SIDE BAR IN GOOGLE DOCS
Detailed Mechanics
1. Starting A Level
Level starts with a 6x6 empty game board.
The level designer will indicate which left most square tile will be the first tile that starts the combo, if tiles are not placed here, There are no combos and only Singular attacks.
Players are presented with a staging area with 3 random tiles at start. They can use these tiles on their board or sell them, or they can press the refresh button which costs silver to be dealt three more random tiles. Pressing the fight buttons begins the battle phase. The tiles themselves are free, only refresh costs money.
Tiles that remain on the board when the refresh button is pressed are sold automatically for 10 gold each.
Once the battle phase starts, the character automatically executes the fighting sequence based on the tiles placed. The enemies will approach from the right side of the screen. If combos are not present on the board, then the player will perform one attack each of punch and/or kicks and/or special attacks if those action tiles exist. There is a 0.6 seconds delay between these attack animations, and these tiles that are not part of the combo will have an attack power penalty. So for example if a combo does not exist, but There are P K and S tiles on the board, the player will do Punch (basic jab animation) → 0.6 second delay → Kick (basic roundhouse kick animation) → 0.6 second delay → Special attack (fireball) → 0.6 second delay → repeat
When the monster crosses the green line seen below, the character will automatically execute the fighting combo. When the monster crosses the red line, they will start to attack the player.
If There are no monsters within melee range of the player, the player will execute a ranged attack based on the total special attack power, with a 0.8 seconds delay between each attack. (Fireball Hadouken animation)
Fireball will hit 3 enemies before disappearing. This can be upgraded. So in this case we can upgrade a fireball to hit the left most 6 enemies.
Players will gain experience and silver from killing monsters. Experience will allow the player to level up within the game and select some random upgrades. Silver is used to obtain more tiles during the preparation phase.
When the wave of monsters is defeated, the camera shifts back down exposing the staging area and we are back to the preparation phase where players get to acquire more tiles and optimize their placements on the board. The game ends in a loss if the player is defeated and HP reaches 0.
The game ends in victory if the player defeats all waves of monsters.
PLEASE NOTE THAT THE AMOUNT OF SILVER AND EXP RECEIVED IS NOT BASED ON MONSTER TYPE KILLED OR QUANTITY OF MONSTERS KILLED. Instead, we are introducing a system that allows designers to set the amount of exp and silver a player will receive each wave, and we divide that across the monsters in that wave..
Block Merging & Rearrangement
When the preparation phase starts, There will be 3 blocks spawned in the bottom area to place or merge.
Holding a piece will show possible placements with highlighted corners.
When the tiles have mergeable counterparts in the board, the mergeable tile on the board will have a glowing outline.
Like the video below.
ScreenRecording_11-11-2025 16-11-07_1.MP4
While arranging the placement of blocks, players can move board tiles to the bottom area and rearrange them back and forth.
The only limitation is that 3 blocks can be stored on the bottom part.
Once players decide to continue fighting, clicking the “Fight” button, the pieces left on the bottom would be sold automatically.
Players can merge the blocks in the bottom part.
2. Combat Power and Damage Calculation
There are three types of action tiles: Punch (P), Kick (K) and Special Attack (S). The corresponding tile colors are green, blue, and red.
Tiles will display the full combat power they provide. Not penalized discounted power.
Tiles will come in different shapes
Punch has a base attack power of 10, Kick is 20, and Special Attack is 40
The same tiles can be merged and upgraded to increase their power. Tiles that are not part of a combo and only contribute half power are called “Assist Tiles,” they are dimmed visually. When merged it simply sums the combat power. So level 1 Punch = 10, level 2 punch = 20, level 3 punch = 40 (Requires 2x level 2) They do not need to be connected to any pieces to contribute. They just need to be on the board.
The individual power of the combo is shown in the UI like seen here below.
The damage per attack sequence is based on the only combo on the board, each board can only have a max of one combo, and for each action in the combo, the damage dealt is calculated using the following:
[Action Power] = [Tile Power + (50%*(SUM of assist tile power))] * Combo Bonus Multiplier
This calculates the individual action power for the combo
Combo multipliers are pre-assigned by game designers. Here is an example of a combo calculation.
Small sample list of combos and their multiplier and base DPS, this is accessed via the info button during the game. The character at the top animates the combo punching air/dummy when the player selects a combo.
3. Combo Creation UI/UX
4. Game Currencies and Homescreen Upgrades
There will be 3 different upgradeable stats at the home screen which are persistent across sessions and levels. The currency used to upgrade is gold. We can consider adding an ad watch when players run out of gold.
They will be extended with gears or other upgrades that we can use later on. So for the implementation, please be aware that we can extend upgrades.
Attack Increase (+2% per upgrade. Additive) So 100% + 2% + 2% + 2% + 2% (Level 4 = 108% * attack)
Health Increase (+2% per upgrade. Additive) Same as attack. So level 5 health increase = 110% * base HP of 100 = 110 total Hp
Health Regen Increase (+0.02% per second, Additive) So level 7 is 2% base regen + (0.02% * 7 = 0.14%) final health regen = 2.14% HP regen per second.
5. Monsters, Stats, Damage Assignment, Stagger and Loot
Each monster when hit is “stunned” for 0.25 seconds. However this has a cooldown of 1.5 seconds. This means after being stunned, the earliest the next time the same monster can be stunned again is 1.25 seconds later because 1.5 second cooldown from first stun - 0.25 stun duration = 1.25 seconds after end of first stun.
Monster attack animation should be from start to finish should be 1 second, with damage dealt at 0.8 second timestamp
We do not need more than 5 monsters for MVP
When monsters are hit, we display damage dealt using standard RPG text VFX. We then display the monster health bar permanently above their head, but we do not display numerical values for their HP
Monster speed is the second it takes to move from edge of screen to crossing the monster attack line. Attack speed is expressed in seconds per attack.

6. Levels
We need to let designers designate starting positions for each level.
Each level will also have obstacles that need to be removed via silver.
Each level will have 15 waves of monsters
Each wave of monsters will get an HP and damage multiplier bonus following a standard algorithm
HP multiplier for monster is wave # * XXX
Damage multiplier for monster is wave # * YYY
We need to utilize the monster spawning system from Zombie Match, this will allow designers to specify monsters spawn timing and quantity
Level Design Tools
Each level will have monsters, monsters spawn, their stats, board type, and the pool of tiles available.

7. Player Starting Stats
Base player HP is 100
Base player regen rate is 2% per second, but this is only during the “fight” phase and not the prep phase.
Base attack is 0, no tiles placed = no damage.
8. Experience Table and Skill Choices
For XP tables Combo Fighter Design Details
For Silver Tables Combo Fighter Design Details
XP and Silver.png
Experience points will reset after each attempt, meaning that it will start from the scratch in every level attempt.
Experience will be gained from the actions below,
Merging blocks yield less XP
Killing enemies yields more XP
Roguelite skills don't require any currency to use. Just selecting the desired one out of all 3 options.
The skills will have 3 phases that can be improved further after selecting the first phase.
Roguelite Skills In MVP
Increase Punch Damage by 35%   (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.) But for this one I think keeping it at +35% regardless of level is a better start.
Increase Kick Damage by 20%   (Can have levels I, II, III, IV, etc.) But for this one I think keeping it at +20% regardless of level is a better start.

Replacement", "description": "**Description:**
Currently, we have many event icons displayed on the main screen. To improve clarity and user navigation, we can adopt a grouping approach similar to *Royal Match*.

**Proposed Change:**

* Group **only-reward events** (e.g., Zombie Lane, Season Pass, Quests) on one side (e.g., right).
* Keep **playable events** on the opposite side (e.g., left).
* Alternatively, we can switch sides — placement order is flexible as long as the grouping remains consistent.

**Goal:**
Improve UI organization and help players quickly identify different event types.

![image.png]([URL_52778])

**Acceptance Criteria:**

* Event icons are consistently grouped by type.
* UI remains balanced and visually clear.
* No loss of functionality or discoverability for any event.
* The order of them is consistent when another event icon is not visible. 

**Adjustable Parameters:**

Since we need to test how it looks in the game. We need certain adjustable parameters for next iterations. 

* The group of an event
* The interchangeable placement for different groups (we can make right icons in the left for later)
* The order of an event within its group", "priority": 3, "estimate": null, "due_date": null, "started_at": "2025-08-12T18:39:58Z", "completed_at": "2025-09-02T13:29:57Z", "canceled_at": null, "archived_at": null, "time_in_status_minutes": 236524, "labels": ["UI", "Improvement"], "links": [], "relations": [], "is_archived": false, "created_at": "2025-08-11T14:53:14Z", "updated_at": "2025-09-02T13:29:57Z"}, {"id": "ZOM-485", "project_id": "dbab77c7-f871-4888-abf8-d98b52a41624", "team_id": "team_ZOM", "parent_id": null, "assignee_id": "usr_EMPLOYEE_0032", "creator_id": "usr_Robert", "state_id": "Done", "cycle_id": null, "identifier": "ZOM-485", "number": 485, "title": "Update endless wave algorithm beyond designer waves", "description": "'@[PERSON_NAME_0054] said:

#### **1. Inventory Data Capture on Player Login to the backend:**

* When a player logs into the backend, capture and send the following for each card:
  * `player_id`
  * `card_id` (integer)
  * `card_level`
    * `0` = Not owned / Locked
    * `1-5` = Owned, corresponds to card level
  * `timestamp` of the login

#### **2. BigQuery Sync:**

* Send this card inventory data to **BigQuery once per day**, ideally on first login of the day.
* Each row in the table should represent a unique player–card inventory.

#### **3. Lookup Table for Card Metadata:**

* Create a **separate BigQuery table** mapping `card_id` → `card_name` (or human-readable identifier).

---

### **Data Schema:**

**Player Card Inventory Table (card_inventory):**

`player_id (string) card_id (int) card_level (int) timestamp (datetime)`

**Card Metadata Table (card_metadata) :**

`card_id (int) card_name (string)`

This means by level 40, a player can easily be labeled as tier 4, which is often the case given how easy our game is early on.

However many of our levels only have 2 tiers of difficult, 0 and 1. And the idea is that if a player loses 4 in a row, they get demoted a player tier. So 4 -> 3 -> 2 and -> 1. However this creates a problem.

A player is difficulty tier 4, plays a difficulty tier 1 level, gets stuck, loses 4 in a row, they are demoted to tier 3. They still load difficulty tier 1 level, and continues to lose. A player would need to lose 12 times for them to actually get to difficulty tier 0 for that level. This defeats the whole purpose of downgrading them. Losing 12 in a row will cause a user to churn.

Solution: when a player is demoted, we also need to demote the level difficulty for the level they are currently on.

So if a player is demoted from tier 4 -> 3, and they were playing tier 1 difficulty and failed, that level will load the tier 0 version.

The following level, it will just go back to normal, meaning if a tier 3 level is available, that's the level that will load for the player. Working title is Operation: No Exit. 

Alternate names: Forever Brains, Till Death Loops Us Apart, Last Zom Standing, Match ‘Em Dead

There isn't a lot of art need for this one, just simple pre-level dialogue UIs and perhaps a few differentiators for the level. 

Some brain storm jump points. 

Mechanic #1 Item Dump 

If we want to make the endless mode more about matching, we can go an item dump to the board in fixed intervals. That way, there is a clear fail condition to end the endless of the endless mode and players can be scored based on how long they survived. If the board gets full beyond allowed capacity, we fail. Extra hard if each item dump has different items. 

Pros: Perfect for the match-oriented players. 
Cons: Can get frustrating very quickly. 

Mechanic #2 Zombie Difficulty

input.title: [Combo-Fighters PR #26] Upgrade-ad cooldown merged over unresolved reviewer objection — still live in build
input.description:
Record of state only (not a work assignment) — raised during the Feb 2026 Combo-Fighters review audit. Left unassigned intentionally.

**PR:** harmonygames-Games/Combo-Fighters #26 "Added cooldown to main menu upgrade ad watch"
**Author:** [PERSON_NAME_0067] · **Reviewer:** Oliver Brooks
**Merged:** 2026-01-15 by Oliver Brooks

**Review status:** Oliver submitted CHANGES_REQUESTED (2026-01-15 13:36). He never re-approved. It was merged the same day with the objection standing.

**What the reviewer was pushing back on**
- Review body (design concern): the 5-minute upgrade-ad cooldown is reset when a level completes AND when the player loses. So a player can enter a level, lose quickly, return to the main menu and immediately watch another upgrade ad again — defeating the cooldown.
- Inline, `Assets/Scripts/Managers/GameController.cs`: "We should probably move both of this Memory lines to WinScreen."

**Author's response:** argued the point — replied that [EMPLOYEE_0016] "mentioned it does not matter if the player win or lose the level," and did not change the behavior. (Reviewer argued with, not ignored.)

**What actually landed (verified at merged head 9ecdc51):** both `GameController.GameRoutine` (win path) and `LoseScreen.Start` (loss path) still call `Memory.SetUpgradeAdWatchedCooldown(reset: true)`. The reset-on-loss behaviour Oliver flagged is present in the build players are on right now.

**Status: OBJECTION STILL STANDING — live in production.** No sign-off was ever recorded.

input.title: [Combo-Fighters PR #35] Blake/backend (auth/profile/store) — author self-merged over reviewer's CHANGES_REQUESTED
input.description:
Record of state only (not a work assignment) — raised during the Feb 2026 Combo-Fighters review audit. Left unassigned intentionally.

**PR:** harmonygames-Games/Combo-Fighters #35 "Blake/backend"
**Author:** Arthur Blake · **Reviewer:** Oliver Brooks
**Merged:** 2026-01-30 21:33 by Arthur Blake (the author)

**Review status:** Oliver submitted CHANGES_REQUESTED (2026-01-30 20:36). Arthur commented at 21:27 and merged his own PR ~6 minutes later at 21:33. Oliver never approved.

**What the reviewer was pushing back on**
- `Assets/Store/DominoPlayerPrefs.cs`: "Can we rename this to something else?" — Arthur replied "Yes" (agreed to the change).
- `Assets/Scripts/UI/Profile/ProfileScreen.cs`: "missing `private`".
- `Assets/Scripts/UI/Profile/ProfileScreen.cs` (x2): "Looks dangerous…. If `_statPrefab` doesn't contain a `ProfileStat`, it will be instantiated and ignored." Recommended making `_statPrefab` a typed `ProfileStat` field and removing the GetComponent/null-guard.

**What actually landed (verified at merged head f065d1ca):**
- Rename: DONE. The class is now `Assets/Store/HarmonyPlayerPrefs.cs` (DominoPlayerPrefs no longer exists). The agreed change landed.
- ProfileScreen prefab safety: NOT addressed as recommended. `_statPrefab` is still an untyped `GameObject`; `AddStat` now does `go.GetComponent<ProfileStat>()` then `stat.Init(...)` with NO null guard → NullReferenceException if a prefab without a ProfileStat is assigned. Leftover `Debug.Log` diagnostic calls also shipped in the AddStat overloads.

**Status:** Rename resolved. Prefab-safety concern UNRESOLVED in the shipped code. Author self-merged own PR without reviewer sign-off. No approval recorded.

input.title: [Combo-Fighters PR #37] Combo Definition Updates — merged without formal re-approval (reviewer's concerns addressed in code)
input.description:
Record of state only (not a work assignment) — raised during the Feb 2026 Combo-Fighters review audit. Left unassigned intentionally.

**PR:** harmonygames-Games/Combo-Fighters #37 "Combo Definition Updates"
**Author:** [PERSON_NAME_0067] · **Reviewer:** Oliver Brooks
**Merged:** 2026-02-13 by Oliver Brooks

**Review status:** Oliver submitted CHANGES_REQUESTED (2026-02-12). No formal APPROVE was ever recorded before it merged the next day. On paper this looks unresolved — but the code tells a different story (see below).

**What the reviewer was pushing back on**
- `Assets/Scripts/ScriptableObjects/ComboDefinition.cs`: (1) `Locked` should not be a stored field on the ScriptableObject — use a computed availability property; (2) drop the `LevelMultiplierRow` class, use a `float[]` indexed by level; (3) enum naming — prefix with E (`ERarityEnum`).
- `Assets/Scripts/UI/ComboScreen.cs`: why is it `_specialPrefab` and not `_lockedPrefab`?
- `Assets/Scripts/UI/LockedComboCell.cs`: replace per-rarity functions with a rarity-data class + `SerializedDictionary`.
- `ComboRarityData.cs` / `ComboRarityDefinition.cs`: "Is this used?" / "Why do we need this?"

**Author's response:** argued the point — engaged on each item and cited "Combo Unlocking Specs" to justify the rarity SOs. (Reviewer argued with, not ignored.)

**What actually landed (verified at merged head bf4e630):** the reviewer's structural feedback WAS implemented — enum renamed to `ERarityEnum`; `Locked` is now computed (`IsLocked => !ComboManager.Instance.IsComboUnlocked(Id)`, not stored); the `LevelMultiplierRow` class was removed (leveling now via `ComboLevelUpData`); rarity visuals moved to a `SerializedDictionary`. The class was renamed `SpecialComboCell`.

**Status:** Concerns effectively RESOLVED in the shipped code; the only gap is that no formal approval was recorded. No code action believed necessary — recording for traceability. (Separate design note: the shipped `ERarityEnum` is Rare/Epic/Legendary/Mythic with no "Common" tier — see the design-spec finding in the audit summary.)

Record of state only (not a work assignment) — raised during the Feb 2026 Combo-Fighters review audit. Left unassigned intentionally.

**PR:** harmonygames-Games/Combo-Fighters #19 "Added anim sequence on combo changed"
**Author:** [PERSON_NAME_0067] · **Reviewer:** Oliver Brooks
**Merged:** 2025-12-30 by Oliver Brooks

**Review status:** Oliver submitted CHANGES_REQUESTED (2025-12-30 18:51). Never re-approved; merged ~1h later. The author did not reply in the thread — nobody said a word.

**What the reviewer was pushing back on** — `Assets/Scripts/VFX/ElectricityController.cs`:
- "Won't this fail when `i` is `comboTiles.Count - 1`? It would probably throw index out of range exception." — pointing at `var next = comboTiles[i + 1];` accessed before the bounds check inside `for (i = 0; i < comboTiles.Count; i++)`.
- "Don't use `?` with MonoBehaviours… check `if (i != comboTiles.Count - 1)` and draw the ray inside that scope without null-checks."

**What actually landed (verified at merged head e6df907):** the buggy block was removed. `ComboSequenceCoroutine` was rewritten so the loop starts at `i = 1` and only references `comboTiles[i]` (always a valid index); the `next` variable and the beam-draw/`Show` calls are commented out. The crash Oliver flagged is NOT in the shipped code.

**Status:** RESOLVED in code despite no reply and no formal approval — recording for traceability. Minor note: the electricity beam drawn between combo tiles was dropped in the rewrite (a functional/visual simplification, not a crash); worth a quick design confirmation that this was intended.

This PR was merged on 2026-01-15 while a `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review from @EMPLOYEE_0003_GITHUB_USERNAME was still standing — no approval was ever posted afterward.

Recorded for the freeze as **objection standing / in production**. Tracking ticket: **ENG-2438** (unassigned — recording state, not assigning work).

So the concerns were effectively resolved in code — only the formal approval is missing; no code action needed. Recorded as **ENG-2440** (unassigned). Design note: the shipped `ERarityEnum` is Rare/Epic/Legendary/Mythic with no "Common" tier, and the rarity/unlock system is not written up in the GDD or the Combo Fighter Design Details sheet — see the audit summary.

input.text:
Arthur — Combo Fighter freeze record, done the way you asked. I went through every PR on `harmonygames-Games/Combo-Fighters`, and for the ones I flag I checked what actually landed on the branch after the reviewer complained, not just the review status. Every flagged PR has a comment on the PR itself and one matching Engineering ticket (unassigned — recording state, not assigning work). Full breakdown:

*THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST — objection still standing, sitting in the live build*

*PR #26 — "Added cooldown to main menu upgrade ad watch"* (author [PERSON_NAME_0067], reviewer Oliver Brooks) → ENG-2438
Oliver requested changes and never re-approved; merged the same day. His concern: the 5-minute upgrade-ad cooldown gets reset both when a level is won AND when it's lost. So a player can drop into a level, lose on purpose in a few seconds, back out to the menu, and immediately watch another upgrade ad — the cooldown does nothing. The author *argued the point* — said [EMPLOYEE_0016] told him it doesn't matter whether you win or lose — and didn't change the code. I checked the merged head: `GameController.GameRoutine` and `LoseScreen.Start` both still call `SetUpgradeAdWatchedCooldown(reset: true)`. This is real and it's in the build people are paying into right now.

*Author self-merged over a standing review*

*PR #35 — "Blake/backend"* (auth / profile / store — your PR, Arthur; reviewer Oliver Brooks) → ENG-2439
Oliver posted CHANGES_REQUESTED at 20:36; you replied and merged your own PR ~6 min later at 21:33 with no approval. Two outcomes:
• The `DominoPlayerPrefs` rename you said "Yes" to *did land* — it's now `HarmonyPlayerPrefs.cs`. (So the one thing that was agreed actually shipped — that's the good version of that story.)
• The one Oliver called "dangerous" did *not* get fixed: `ProfileScreen._statPrefab` is still an untyped `GameObject`, and `AddStat` does `GetComponent<ProfileStat>()` then `stat.Init(...)` with no null check → NullReferenceException if the wrong prefab is ever dragged in. His suggested typed-field fix wasn't taken. A couple of `Debug.Log` lines shipped too.

*Went in without a sign-off, BUT the code was actually fixed — no action needed, just recording so nobody re-opens a ghost*

*PR #37 — "Combo Definition Updates"* (author [PERSON_NAME_0067], reviewer Oliver Brooks) → ENG-2440
Author *argued the points* (and cited "Combo Unlocking Specs" — see the design note below). No formal approval before merge, so on paper it looks unresolved — but at the merged head every structural ask was implemented: enum renamed to `ERarityEnum`, `Locked` is now computed instead of a stored field, the `LevelMultiplierRow` class is gone (leveling moved to `ComboLevelUpData`), rarity visuals moved to a `SerializedDictionary`. Effectively resolved; only the sign-off is missing.

*PR #19 — "Added anim sequence on combo changed"* (author [PERSON_NAME_0067], reviewer Oliver Brooks) → ENG-2441
This is the "*nobody said a word*" one — Oliver flagged an IndexOutOfRange (`comboTiles[i + 1]` read before the bounds check) and the author never replied in the thread, merged ~1h later. But the code got fixed anyway: the coroutine was rewritten to loop from `i = 1` and only touch valid indices; the crashing block is commented out. Not in the shipped build. (One side effect worth a design nod: the electricity beam drawn *between* tiles was dropped in that rewrite.)

*"Agreed then never landed" — the worst kind*
You specifically asked me to call this out on its own. I found *no* case of someone agreeing to a change that then silently didn't ship. The only explicit agreement in the set was your "Yes" to the rename on #35, and that one did land.

*Signed off before merge — process worked, leaving alone*
PR #24 (AppLovin/Rewarded Ads) got a real APPROVE from Oliver after two rounds of changes, then merged. #9, #16, #22 were approved too. Nothing to do on these.

*Design side vs what shipped (the spec you pointed at)*
You remembered pointing at a spec during one of these reviews and weren't sure it says what you said. Here's the honest answer: on #37 the rarity work was defended with "Combo Unlocking Specs," but there is no such spec. I read the *Combo Fighter GDD* and every tab of *Combo Fighter Design Details* — combos are only defined there as damage-multiplier entries. There is no rarity/unlock system written down at all (no Common/Rare/Epic/Legendary/Mythic tiers, no unlock costs, no per-rarity level tables). The rarity tiers actually came out of *this channel* on Feb 12–13 ("Rare, Legendary, Mythical, Epic — four kinds?"). And what shipped — `ERarityEnum { Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythic }`, no "Common" — doesn't even match the one concrete example quoted in the #37 review, which started with a Common tier (100/200/300). So: the design docs do *not* back up what shipped, because the rarity/unlock design was never actually written down. If we want it on paper it needs writing from scratch.

*Zombie Match board cleanup*
Went through the urgent (P1) tickets. Two were dev-complete ("In Validation") and stale ~4 months, both labeled "Hot Fix - Global Launch" — clearly shipped and just never closed, so I closed them:
• ZOM-668 "Make sure event tokens are doubled" → Done
• ZOM-618 "Rewarded Ad Implementation" → Done
The other urgent ones I *left open* because they're genuinely not done — ZOM-611 (In Progress), ZOM-608 (Regression), and ZOM-667 / 591 / 535 / 438 (still Todo). Didn't want to bury live problems as "done."
